Biomechanics instruments report a mixture of direct observations and quantities
derived through calibration, geometry, signal processing, or a physical model.
This hub points to articles that examine those layers. A summary here is an
editorial description of the linked article; it is not independent evidence for
that article's equations, numbers, causal interpretation, or validation state.

::: {.callout-important}
## State and Editorial Contract

**Available** means the linked article can be read. It does not mean every claim
on the page is validated. Each article must identify what is measured, derived,
estimated, simulated, or proposed; name its sources and assumptions; and retain
its own uncertainty, falsifiers, and audience limits. Until that page's
route-level audit is protected-closed, treat its scientific conclusions as
page-specific and not inherited by this hub.
:::

## Measurement Guides

### [Force Measurement Technology](../articles/technology-force-measurement.html)

**Article state: Available.** Surveys force plates, pressure mats, wrench and
centre-of-pressure conventions, calibration, and instrument limitations. Device
specifications and performance claims require the sources and conditions on the
article page.

### [Motion Capture Technology](../articles/technology-motion-capture.html)

**Article state: Available.** Surveys marker-based, markerless, inertial, and
imaging methods, including calibration, coordinate conventions, and error
sources. No modality is declared universally accurate by this hub.

### [Launch Monitor Technology](../articles/technology-launch-monitors.html)

**Article state: Available.** Surveys radar and photometric methods and separates
direct observations from inferred club and ball quantities. Vendor behavior and
accuracy remain device-, firmware-, protocol-, and condition-specific.

### [Launch Monitor Vendor Reference](../articles/launch-monitor-vendor-reference.html)

**Article state: Available.** Indexes public vendor documentation and parameter
definitions. It is a source map, not certification, an endorsement, or proof
that identically named fields are numerically interchangeable.

## Modeling and Analysis Guides

### [Club Fitting Simulation and Parameter Identification](../articles/technology-club-fitting.html)

**Article state: Available; engineering workflow experimental.** Describes
counterfactual club-model changes, shaft and inertia representations, and data
interchange. A deterministic computation is still conditional on its model,
parameters, solver, input trajectory, and validation envelope.

### [Multibody Impact Coupling and the Heavy Hit Hypothesis](../articles/technology-heavy-hit-impact-coupling.html)

**Article state: Available; hypothesis scope model-conditioned.** Examines
short-duration impact, wave-transit and multibody-coupling arguments. Read the
linked derivation and limitations before applying any result to a person, club,
impact condition, or coaching claim.

### [The Reference-Point Problem in Club Delivery Data](../articles/reference-point-problem.html)

**Article state: Available.** Examines how a reported velocity or path depends on
the selected point on a rotating clubhead. Numerical examples remain conditional
on the declared geometry and measurement convention.

### [Impact Mechanics and Ball Flight](../articles/impact-mechanics-and-ball-flight.html)

**Article state: Available.** Surveys collision and flight models, their
parameters, and disagreements. Worked predictions are model outputs, not a
universal launch-monitor or player result.

### [Rotation-Induced Spin](../articles/rotation-induced-spin.html)

**Article state: Available; bounded model result.** Develops a rigid-contact
calculation for a rotating face and brackets it with contact assumptions. The
physical result depends on whether those assumptions describe the impact.

### [The Physics of the Rolling Putt](../articles/putting-roll-models.html)

**Article state: Available.** Derives idealized impact, skid, roll, slope, and
capture models. Parameters and course conditions bound any numerical prediction.

### [Simulating the Green](../articles/green-simulation.html)

**Article state: Available; software and stochastic extensions experimental.**
Describes how idealized roll equations, event handling, surfaces, and uncertainty
can be represented in software. Simulated make regions are not validated player
make rates.

## Shared Geometry, Bounded

Rigid-body twist and wrench notation provides a useful common language for
motion and load measurements, and their reciprocal product has units of power
when both are expressed at compatible points and in compatible frames. That
mathematical pairing does not make every instrument a direct six-dimensional
observer: sensors expose different projections, bandwidths, calibrations, and
model dependencies. Instrument-specific observability and validation remain the
authority for what can be inferred.
